phase3_findings.description: docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md:120 says a call cancelled while queued never runs, and the run_memory_call docstring says a caller cancelled before its call starts drops it; asyncio.wrap_future cancels the executor future from a call_soon-scheduled done callback, so the single worker can start the queued call in that gap.
Test stubs (_StoreCalls._enter, _held_call, held_iter_all) ignore the return value of held.wait(HOLD_LIMIT_S), so a hold timeout is not reported.

store.py executor rationale comment gives only the object.__new__ test reason, omits that server.py builds two MemoryStore instances, and names a 'store's own executor' MemoryStore does not have (it is ChromaAgentMemory's).
transport.md:119 names 'the store's own two-thread executor' (it is ChromaAgentMemory's) and says last_skipped_rows is shared by every caller, which holds only per instance.
The one-store-call-at-a-time rule is enforced only by convention; MemoryStore's synchronous methods remain public and callable from any thread.
run_memory_call's Callable[P, T] -> T signature accepts generator functions, lazy iterators and async callables whose store work would not run on the worker.
_baseline docstring guarantee is accurate but does not cover async per-entry writes on ChromaAgentMemory's executor, ordered only by the handlers' asyncio.Locks.
Overlap test covers only export/list/stats; import_bundle's baseline and clear_memories are never run concurrently with a read tool.
No test checks that a call cancelled while waiting in the memory worker queue is dropped.
The 'never runs' cancellation claim in transport.md:120 and the run_memory_call docstring is absolute though a race window exists between task cancel and the wrap_future done callback.
Loop-side test replaces server_module.json with a namespace holding only dumps and asserts exactly seven calls, which is brittle to future json use.
